rows.event: Ziraat Bankasi vs Gaziantep Genclik Spor
flags: Unanimous four-tip market; two expert tipsters; no event-level official extraction
rows.prediction: Ziraat Bankasi to beat Gaziantep Genclik Spor. All four OLBG tips back the Ankara side and two expert tipsters are involved, the strongest unanimous read on the Turkish card. Ziraat's serving and block depth have overwhelmed lower-blocking teams in the early rounds, while Gaziantep's reception unit cracks under sustained pressure. Selection: Ziraat Bankasi to win the match.

flags: No event-level official extraction
rows.prediction: Halkbank Ankara to win at TFL Altekma. Four of five OLBG tips take the visitors, one of the most established clubs in the Turkish league, whose roster depth and Champions League-level experience dwarf a smaller Altekma programme. Home support keeps the first set interesting, but Halkbank's serving should take over from the second set onward. Selection: Halkbank Ankara to win.

flags: Expert tipster attached; no event-level official extraction
rows.prediction: Bergamo W to beat Marignano W in Serie A1. Five of seven OLBG tips, including an expert tipster, favour a Bergamo side whose outside hitting and block timing have looked the more polished unit in the opening weeks. Marignano rely on a narrow serving game that Bergamo's passers are well placed to neutralise. Selection: Bergamo to win the match.

flags: Expert tipster attached; no event-level official extraction
rows.prediction: VaLePa to beat AC Oulu. Three of four OLBG tips, including an expert, back the home side, a traditional powerhouse of the Finnish league with a clear edge in middle-blocking and serve reception. Oulu's young roster is competitive in stretches but rarely sustains it across four or five sets on the road. Selection: VaLePa to win.

flags: South American fixture outside CEV remit; no event-level official extraction
rows.prediction: Praia Clube to beat Sao Jose at home. Three of four OLBG tips back the Uberlandia club, whose continental-level roster and home arena make them a reliable force in the Brazilian women's league. Sao Jose's transition game struggles against organised block defences of Praia's quality. Selection: Praia Clube to win, medium confidence given the four-tip sample.

rows.prediction: Paris Saint-Germain to beat Aalborg at home. The EHF match list confirms the Champions League fixture, while OLBG's headline 'Tie' call reflects an anomalous market pattern across this round rather than a read on PSG's strength. PSG's home court and deep back-court rotation make them the cleaner match-winner proposition against an Aalborg side that travels well but rarely controls sixty minutes in Paris. Selection: PSG match winner, medium confidence.

rows.prediction: SC Magdeburg to beat HC Kriens-Luzern. The official EHF page confirms the contest, and the gap in squad depth between a Champions League knockout regular in Magdeburg and a first-season-level Kriens project is substantial. OLBG's tie-heavy board is treated as a market irregularity; at home, Magdeburg's pressing defence and pivot play should decide a game they are better built to control. Selection: Magdeburg match winner.

rows.prediction: Industria Kielce to beat Kolstad at home. Kielce's experience of deep Champions League nights and a loud hall give them the structural edge over a Kolstad side whose results have depended on a small core firing together. With the OLBG 'Tie' pattern treated cautiously, the home side's goalkeeper variance is the main risk rather than any talent gap. Selection: Kielce match winner, medium confidence.

rows.prediction: FC Barcelona to win away at Skanderborg/Aarhus. The EHF detail page lists the Danish hosts as SAH Aarhus against a Barca side that remains the benchmark of the competition, rotating internationals across every line. The lone OLBG tip on the home side looks like a longshot opinion rather than a consensus. Selection: Barcelona match winner; the short price means confidence is high on outcome but the value lies in game totals instead.

rows.prediction: One Veszprem HC to edge FC Porto, treated as the lowest-confidence play of the handball card. Porto's Dragao Arena is one of the most difficult trips in the group phase, which is why the OLBG board leans to a draw, but Veszprem's individual quality in the back line offers the higher ceiling if the game opens up late. Selection: Veszprem match winner, small stake.
